title: 火锅分几派④完结·贵州酸汤：红汤界的新顶流 | China Hotpot Schools P4 · Guizhou 🍲
description:
麻辣、鲜甜、清水、酸——四派火锅，你到底站哪一派？评论区见。

【火锅分几派·完结篇 贵州酸汤】红汤界最近杀出一个新顶流，来自贵州。它的秘密藏在苗族一句老话——「以酸代盐」：从前山里缺盐，先民就用自然发酵的酸来调味。红酸汤用新鲜番茄和辣椒，装坛密封发酵五六个月，再磨浆又发酵半个月，才熬出那口鲜红醇酸。临锅一勺木姜子，整锅香味瞬间活了；酸辣鲜香，鱼肉入口即化，贵州话喊一声——板扎！「凯里酸汤鱼制作技艺」已是国家级非遗。从重庆的麻辣、潮汕的鲜甜、北京的清水，到贵州的酸——这一桌，就是中国火锅的四种派别。你站哪一派？

A new star has broken into China's red-broth hotpots, and it's from Guizhou. Its secret is an old Miao saying — 'sour instead of salt': short on salt in the mountains, their ancestors seasoned with natural fermentation. Red sour soup ferments fresh tomato and chili in sealed jars for five to six months, then is ground to a pulp and fermented again. A last spoon of litsea (mountain pepper) wakes the whole pot. Sour, spicy, fresh — the fish melts in your mouth. Kaili sour-soup fish is now national intangible heritage. From Chongqing's mala, to Chaoshan's sweetness, to Beijing's plain water, to Guizhou's sour — that's four schools of Chinese hotpot on one table.
